selected.title: The first alert goes to the utility
selected.texas_link: AEP Texas says it is putting AI cameras on communications towers in high-risk parts of its west Texas service territory. The page names no county, so the film draws the Big Country region and says west Texas.

movement.action: reported 16 Pano AI wildfire cameras installed and a target of 56 by February 2027
movement.object: tower-mounted AI cameras in its west Texas service territory

selected.why_today: AEP Texas published its camera count on October 6th, the freshest dated Texas movement on AI in emergency detection that no recent film has covered.
selected.consequence: When a camera detects heat or smoke, the AEP Texas team receives a text or email within an estimated ten minutes, and AEP says it can share that awareness with outside responders.
selected.application_change: A 200-foot communications tower now carries a camera that watches 360 degrees and software that flags heat or smoke, so the utility team learns of a possible fire from a message instead of a passerby.
selected.counter_image: AEP says the cameras do not prevent wildfires, the ten minutes is an estimate, and the page publishes no measured detection or response record.
selected.earned_take: The first message goes to the utility's own team, and AEP publishes an estimate of ten minutes but no measure of how much sooner anyone arrives.

agency.next_step: AEP Texas says it will install toward 56 cameras by February 2027, and its wildfire mitigation plan awaits Public Utility Commission approval for a January 2027 start.
agency.who_can_act: AEP Texas installs the cameras and receives the alerts. The Public Utility Commission of Texas reviews the plan.

sources.note: T&D World, AEP Texas files wildfire mitigation plan
Spectrum News, PUCT wildfire plan filings

filmability.viewer_question: When a camera on a west Texas tower sees smoke, who hears first, and what do they know?
filmability.opening_action: An explanatory diagram labelled Illustration. A tower camera sweeps a dry horizon, a small plume enters the sweep and a flag marks it. No real footage, no AEP site.
filmability.mechanism: Input: a camera on a tall communications tower watching 360 degrees. Transformation: software flags heat or smoke. Result: a text or email reaches the AEP Texas team. Limit: cameras do not prevent fires and no response record is published.
filmability.human_consequence: Residents and landowners in high-risk country and the AEP crew who get the message. AEP reports no major fire response since launch and no measured lead time.
filmability.source_limit: AEP's own community page is the only source for the cameras. The ten minutes is an estimate, no county or launch date is named, and the trade summary of the filed plan does not mention cameras.
three_key_images: Tower camera sweeping dry country (diagram, Illustration)
A flag on a small plume then a message leaving the tower (diagram, Illustration)
The message at the utility team card beside the stated limit that cameras do not prevent fires (diagram, Illustration)

visual_stakes.affected_group: Residents and landowners in AEP Texas's high-risk west Texas territory and the AEP Texas wildfire crew that receives the alert.
visual_stakes.physical_subject: a tower camera sweeping dry country and the flag that leaves it
visual_stakes.visible_change: a plume enters the sweep, a flag appears on it and a message leaves for the utility team
visual_stakes.consequence: AEP estimates its team is notified about ten minutes after detection. No response record is published.
visual_stakes.opening_question: When a tower camera sees smoke, who hears first?
visual_stakes.answer: The utility's own team, by text or email, per AEP Texas. The cameras do not prevent fires.
visual_stakes.asset_fit: Two fresh authored source groups, a tower-camera hero and a supporting dry-country environment, shared by exactly two complete treatments. Diagram and illustration only, no footage, no real site, no crew figure.
visual_stakes.affected_person: A west Texas landowner near a tower and the AEP crew member whose phone gets the message
